name: Satellite antenna SHM benchmark
description: Shape sensing techniques for real-time deformation reconstruction are an increasingly important topic for Structural Health Monitoring (SHM), particularly in the con- text of digitalisation and digital twins. Artificial intelligence and artificial neural net- works are showing promising results for such tasks. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) have recently gained interest due to less training data-dependent predictions by incorporating physics laws into the training. To benchmark such a PINN for solving inverse problems in shape sensing, referred to as “iPINN”, this paper presents a study on its performance against the Modal Method (MM) as an established technique on the example of a composite space antenna. Moreover, a combination of the two mainstream methods for shape sensing is tested on the same space structure. reputation: A niche research benchmark used in the SHM and digital-twin community to compare physics-informed and modal-method shape sensing approaches on a realistic aerospace structure.
notes: Non-LLM, small specialized dataset, and results are highly dependent on sensor placement, structural assumptions, and reconstruction setup.
